test_cases.question: What types of damage can someone claim compensation for under GDPR?
test_cases.answer: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered. Material damage includes financial losses; non-material damage includes emotional distress, reputational harm, and other intangible harms.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Any person who has suffered material or non-material damage as a result of an infringement of this Regulation shall have the right to receive compensation from the controller or processor for the damage suffered

test_cases.question: What is the difference between controller and processor liability under GDPR?
test_cases.answer: Any controller involved in processing shall be liable for the damage caused by processing which infringes this Regulation. A processor has more limited liability - it shall be liable for the damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of this Regulation specifically directed to processors or where it has acted outside or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Any controller involved in processing shall be liable for the damage caused by processing which infringes this Regulation. A processor shall be liable for the damage caused by processing only where it has not complied with obligations of this Regulation specifically directed to processors or where it has acted outside or contrary to lawful instructions of the controller
key_phrases: processor shall be liable... only where

test_cases.question: How can a controller or processor be exempted from liability?
test_cases.answer: A controller or processor shall be exempted from liability if it proves that it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage. The burden of proof is on the controller or processor to demonstrate complete non-responsibility.
test_cases.supporting_quote: A controller or processor shall be exempted from liability under paragraph 2 if it proves that it is not in any way responsible for the event giving rise to the damage

test_cases.question: If multiple parties are responsible for GDPR damage, can a data subject recover the full amount from just one?
test_cases.answer: Yes. Where more than one controller or processor are involved in the same processing and are responsible for any damage, each controller or processor shall be held liable for the entire damage in order to ensure effective compensation of the data subject. This is joint and several liability.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where more than one controller or processor, or both a controller and a processor, are involved in the same processing and where they are... responsible for any damage caused by processing, each controller or processor shall be held liable for the entire damage in order to ensure effective compensation of the data subject
key_phrases: more than one controller or processor

test_cases.question: Can a party who paid full compensation recover from other responsible parties?
test_cases.answer: Yes. Where a controller or processor has paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that controller or processor shall be entitled to claim back from the other controllers or processors involved in the same processing that part of the compensation corresponding to their part of responsibility for the damage.
test_cases.supporting_quote: Where a controller or processor has, in accordance with paragraph 4, paid full compensation for the damage suffered, that controller or processor shall be entitled to claim back from the other controllers or processors involved in the same processing that part of the compensation corresponding to their part of responsibility for the damage

b2b_relevance: CRITICAL - Article 82 is the damages article. Key implications: (1) BOTH material and non-material damages recoverable, (2) Controllers broadly liable for any infringement, (3) Processors only liable for processor-specific obligations OR acting outside instructions, (4) Joint and several liability means one party can pay all, (5) Can recover from co-responsible parties. For B2B SaaS: ensure processor agreements clearly define instructions and allocate liability.
